h: Refining the Evil Inclination and Self Interest

p: וַיְהִי מִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים.
— And it came to pass at the end of two full years.
בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּתְחוּ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ בַּפָּסוּק קֵץ שָׂם לַחֹשֶׁךְ וְגוֹמֵר.
— Midrash Rabbah and the holy Zohar open this portion with the verse, “He sets an end to darkness,” and so forth.
וְאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה שֶׁכָּל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּצֶר הָרָע בָּעוֹלָם אוֹפֶל וְצַלְמָוֶת בָּעוֹלָם, דִּכְתִיב אֶבֶן אֹפֶל וְצַלְמָוֶת.
— Midrash Rabbah says that as long as the evil inclination is in the world, darkness and the shadow of death are in the world, as it is written, “a stone of darkness and the shadow of death.”
נֶעֱקַר יֵצֶר הָרָע מִן הָעוֹלָם, אֵין אוֹפֶל וְצַלְמָוֶת בָּעוֹלָם.
— When the evil inclination is uprooted from the world, there is no darkness or shadow of death in the world.
דָּבָר אַחֵר, קֵץ שָׂם לַחֹשֶׁךְ: זְמַן נָתַן לְיוֹסֵף כַּמָּה שָׁנִים יַעֲשֶׂה בָּאֲפֵלָה וְכוּלֵי.
— Another interpretation of “He sets an end to darkness”: He set a time for Joseph, determining how many years he would spend in darkness, etc.
הָעִנְיָן שֶׁמִּקּוֹדֶם הָיָה יוֹסֵף בַּבּוֹר עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ז.
— The explanation is that Joseph had previously been in the pit for ten years, as stated in Shemos Rabbah, chapter 7.
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם מִסְפַּר עֶשֶׂר מוֹרֶה עַל מִסְפָּר שָׁלֵם, עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת.
— The number ten always indicates a complete number, corresponding to the ten sefirot.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁתִּיקֵּן בְּחִינָתוֹ בְּכָל הָעֶשֶׂר מִדּוֹת.
— This means that he rectified his own aspect in all ten attributes.

h: Joseph and the Counsel of the Serpent

p: וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָיָה עוֹד ב' שָׁנִים, וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: עַל יְדֵי שֶׁאָמַר לְשַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים זְכַרְתַּנִי וְהִזְכַּרְתַּנִי, נִתּוֹסֵף לוֹ ב' שָׁנִים.
— He then remained another two years. Bereishis Rabbah says that because he told the chief cupbearer, “remember me” and “mention me,” two years were added to his imprisonment.
וּבְוַדַּאי לֹא בָּטַח יוֹסֵף חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בְּשַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים, וַהֲרֵי דָּרְשׁוּ: אַשְׁרֵי הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר שָׂם הַשֵּׁם מִבְטַחוֹ, זֶה יוֹסֵף.
— Joseph certainly did not place his trust in the chief cupbearer, Heaven forbid. Indeed, the Sages interpret “Happy is the man who makes Hashem his trust” as referring to Joseph.
רַק מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרָאָה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁיְּשׁוּעָתוֹ עֲתִידָה לָבֹא עַל יְדֵי שַׂר הַמַּשְׁקִים, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת בַּסּוֹף, עַל כֵּן אָמַר לוֹ כִּי אִם זְכַרְתַּנִי וְגוֹמֵר.
— Rather, he saw through Divine inspiration that his deliverance would come through the chief cupbearer, as ultimately happened. He therefore said to him, “If only you remember me,” and so forth.
אַךְ זֶהוּ עוֹד נְגִיעָה לְעַצְמוֹ, וְזֶהוּ בָּא עַל יְדֵי עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ שֶׁהִכְנִיס בָּאָדָם לְהַרְגִּישׁ הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף.
— Yet this still involved self-interest. It comes from the serpent’s counsel, which implanted in the human being a sensitivity to bodily pleasure.
וְזֶה נֶחְשָׁב לְמַדְרֵגַת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק לְחֵטְא, שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לְפִי מִדָּתוֹ הָיָה לוֹ לְהַנִּיחַ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי יִגְמוֹר בַּעֲדוֹ לְטוֹבָה בְּלֹא הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ.

— At Joseph the righteous one’s level, this counted as a sin. Given his particular spiritual attribute, he should have left matters to Hashem, who would certainly have brought about a favorable outcome without his own effort.
וְאִיתָא (שַׁבָּת נה:): ד' מֵתוּ בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ וְכוּלֵי.
— It is taught in Shabbat 55b: “Four died through the serpent’s counsel,” etc.
וְכוּלְּהוּ גְּמָרָא לְבַר מִיִּשַׁי אֲבִי דָוִד דִּמְפָרֵשׁ בֵּיהּ קְרָא, דִּכְתִיב בַּת נָחָשׁ וְכוּלֵי.
— All these cases are known through received tradition except for Yishai, David’s father, whose case Scripture itself explains: “the daughter of Nachash,” etc.
בַּת מִי שֶׁמֵּת בְּעֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ וְכוּלֵי, וְקָרֵי לֵיהּ נָחָשׁ.
— It means the daughter of one who died through the serpent’s counsel, etc.; thus Scripture calls him “Nachash,” the serpent.
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ): הֵן בְּעָווֹן חוֹלָלְתִּי, בְּעָווֹן מָלֵא (כֵּן הוּא גִּרְסַת יַלְקוּט תְּהִלִּים).

— This follows Midrash Rabbah at the beginning of Tazria: “Behold, I was formed in iniquity”—the Hebrew word for “iniquity” being written in full, with two vavs (this is the reading in Yalkut Tehillim).
אֲפִלּוּ אִם יִהְיֶה חָסִיד שֶׁבַּחֲסִידִים, אִי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ צַד א' מֵעָוֹן וְכוּלֵי.
— Even if he is the most pious of the pious, it is impossible that there be no element of iniquity in him, etc.
וְזֶה עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ, שֶׁהִכְנִיס הַנָּחָשׁ בְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁיַּרְגִּישׁ הֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ.
— This is the serpent’s counsel: the serpent instilled in Adam the sensation of his own pleasure.
וְעַל כֵּן אַחַר שֶׁבֵּירֵר יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּכָל הַמִּדּוֹת, הָיָה לוֹ עֵסֶק עוֹד לְבָרֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ בְּעִנְיַן עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ.
— Therefore, after Joseph the righteous one refined himself in all the attributes, he still had to refine himself regarding the serpent’s counsel.

וְאַחַר שֶׁבֵּירֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ בִּב' הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת וְזָכָה לִהְיוֹת קֵץ שָׂם לַחֹשֶׁךְ, שֶׁנֶּעֱקַר יֵצֶר הָרָע מִלִּבּוֹ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה לוֹ עוֹד עֵסֶק בָּעוֹלָם, שֶׁהֲרֵי חַי אַחַר כָּךְ פ' שָׁנָה.

— After refining himself on these two levels and attaining “He sets an end to darkness,” with the evil inclination uprooted from his heart, he nevertheless still had work in the world: he lived another eighty years.
וְכָל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם עֵסֶק, כְּשֶׁנִּשְׁלָם לְגַמְרֵי אֵין לוֹ חַיִּים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לֹא אוּכַל עוֹד לָצֵאת וְלָבֹא.
— Someone who has no remaining work, having reached complete perfection, has no further life in this world, as it is said, “I can no longer go out and come in.”

אֲבָל כָּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עֵסֶק עוֹד, אַף שֶׁחַי שֶׁלֹּא בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע, מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ לוֹ חַיִּים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, דִּכְתִיב וַיְחִי יַעֲקֹב, וְאִיתָא (סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ה) שֶׁזָּכָה לְחַיִּים שֶׁלֹּא בְּצַעַר וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע.

— But one who still has work continues living in this world even without an evil inclination. So we find concerning our forefather Jacob, of whom it says, “And Jacob lived”; Seder Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 5, says that he attained life without suffering and without the evil inclination.
וּמְלַמְּדֵנוּ בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ שֶׁעִיקַּר עֵסֶק הָאָדָם לִהְיוֹת קֵץ שָׂם לַחֹשֶׁךְ, לְשָׁרֵשׁ אֶת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע מִלִּבּוֹ.
— This portion teaches us that a person’s primary task is “to set an end to darkness,” uprooting the evil inclination from his heart.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ יֵשׁ לוֹ עוֹד עֵסֶק לְתַקֵּן עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ, שֶׁהוּא הַנְּגִיעָה לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ.
— Afterward he still has to rectify the serpent’s counsel, the bias toward his own pleasure.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 89:3: “‘Happy is the man who has made the Lord his trust’ (Psalms 40:5) – this is Joseph. ‘And did not turn to the proud’ (Psalms 40:5) – because he said to the chief butler: ‘Remember me…and mention me,’ two years were added for him. ‘Happy is the man who makes the Lord his trust’ – Rabbi Yudan said: Many myriads of myriads tend after falsehood, woe unto anyone who puts his trust in them. ‘For a dream comes with a multitude of concerns’ (Ecclesiastes 5:2) – Pharaoh said: ‘Who stands over whom – I for my god, or my god over me?’ (Joseph) said to him: ‘You, over your god.’ That is what is written: ‘It was at the conclusion (of two years, and Pharaoh was dreaming: and, behold, he stood at the Nile.)’ ‘For he emerged from prison to reign’ (Ecclesiastes 4:14) – this is Joseph, who emerged from Pharaoh’s prison. ‘Emerged…to reign’ – ‘Pharaoh sent (and summoned Joseph, and they rushed him from the dungeon)’ (Genesis 41:14). ‘For even in his reign, he is revealed as poor’ (Ecclesiastes 4:14) – due to Joseph’s reign, the impoverishment of Potifera was revealed. Another matter, ‘it was at the conclusion.’ ‘I saw all the living, who walk under the sun’ (Ecclesiastes 4:15) – this is Joseph. ‘With the second child’ (Ecclesiastes 4:15) – these are the two years that were added for him. Why were two years added for him? So that Pharaoh would dream and (Joseph) would be elevated by means of the dream, as it is stated: ‘It was at the conclusion of two years.’”

h: The Tree of Life Within Every Fruit

p: וְעִיקַּר הַתִּיקּוּן עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּקְרָא עֵץ הַחַיִּים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (רֵישׁ סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה): אֵין עֵץ הַחַיִּים אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה.
— The principal rectification comes through Torah, called the Tree of Life. As the beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah states, “The Tree of Life is none other than Torah.”
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (ר"ב א): דְּהָא לֵית לָךְ מִלָּה לְתַבְרָא יֵצֶר הָרָע אֶלָּא אוֹרַיְיתָא.
— The holy Zohar on this portion (202a) states, “For you have nothing that can break the evil inclination except Torah.”
וְהִנֵּה כְּבָר אָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּתִקּוּנֵי זֹהַר (תִּיקּוּן כד), וְכֵן בְּתִיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר חָדָשׁ בְּעִנְיַן עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע.
— We have already discussed what Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 24), and likewise Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, say concerning the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil.
חַד אָמַר חִטָּה הָיָה וְחַד אָמַר גֶּפֶן, וְכֹלָּא קְשׁוֹט, שֶׁבַע מִינִין אִינּוּן וְכוּלֵי.
— One says it was wheat and another says it was a vine; “all are true: they are seven species,” etc.
וְלִכְאוֹרָה הֵאֵיךְ יִתָּכֵן שֶׁכּוּלָּם אֱמֶת בִּדְבַר מַחֲלוֹקֶת בַּמְּצִיאוּת?
— How can all the opinions be true when they dispute a matter of fact?
וְאָמַרְנוּ דִּכְתִיב וְעֵץ הַחַיִּים בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן וְעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע.
— We explained that it says, “And the Tree of Life in the midst of the garden, and the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil.”
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַפְּנִימִיּוּת שֶׁבְּכָל עֲצֵי הַגָּן הָיָה עֵץ הַחַיִּים וְעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, וְנִיתַּן כֹּחַ זֶה בָּהֶם.
— The inward essence of all the garden’s trees was the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil; this capacity was placed within them.
שֶׁאִם הָיָה טוֹעֵם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים תְּחִלָּה, הָיָה מַרְגִּישׁ בַּאֲכִילָתוֹ מִכָּל פְּרִי הַגָּן טַעַם עֵץ הַחַיִּים, לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחְמִי, שֶׁהוּא תּוֹרָה.
— Had he tasted the Tree of Life first, he would have sensed its flavor whenever eating any fruit of the garden: “Come, eat of My bread,” meaning Torah.
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁטָּעַם מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת נַעֲשָׂה הָעִרְבּוּב, וְטָעַם בְּכָל אֲכִילָתוֹ מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע.
— But once he tasted the Tree of Knowledge, good and evil became intermingled, and everything he ate carried the taste of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil.
וְהַיְינוּ מַה שֶּׁהִרְגִּישׁ הֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁהוּא עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ. (וְנִתְבָּאֵר בְּרֵאשִׁית מַאֲמָר ח.)
— This is his sensation of his own pleasure, which is the serpent’s counsel. (This was explained in Bereishis, maamar 8.)

Rav Tzadok explains here that the inner capacity of the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge was present in all the trees of the garden. h: Repentance Before the Gifts of Torah

p: וְהִנֵּה אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל כָּתוּב וְעַתָּה פֶּן יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ וְלָקַח גַּם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים וְאָכַל וָחַי לְעוֹלָם.
— After the corruption, it says, “And now, lest he stretch out his hand and take also from the Tree of Life, and eat and live forever.”

וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין מַה יַּזִּיק שֶׁיֹּאכַל מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים וְיִחְיֶה לְעוֹלָם. וּבִפְרָט לְפִי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ דְּעֵץ הַחַיִּים הוּא תּוֹרָה, יֹאכַל מֵהַתּוֹרָה וִיתַקֵּן הַקִּלְקוּל.
— What harm would there be in his eating from the Tree of Life and living forever? Especially since Tanna Devei Eliyahu identifies it with Torah: let him partake of Torah and rectify the corruption!
אַךְ הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כא): וְעַתָּה, אֵין וְעַתָּה אֶלָּא תְּשׁוּבָה, וְהוּא אוֹמֵר פֶּן וְאֵין פֶּן אֶלָּא לָאו.
— The answer follows Bereishis Rabbah, chapter 21: “And now” signifies repentance, yet Adam says “pen,” and “pen” signifies a refusal.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁפָּתַח לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פֶּתַח שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה וְלֹא רָצָה לָשׁוּב.
— Hashem opened a door of repentance for him, but he did not wish to repent.
וְאָמַר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: פֶּן בַּהֲסָתַת הַנָּחָשׁ יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ וְלָקַח גַּם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים.
— Hashem therefore said: lest, at the serpent’s instigation, he stretch out his hand and take also from the Tree of Life.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר דִּבְרֵי מְנַחֵם מֵהָרַב הַקָּדוֹשׁ מֵרוֹמָנוֹב עַל הַפָּסוּק וַיִּשְׁלַח אַבְרָהָם אֶת יָדוֹ וַיִּקַּח אֶת הַמַּאֲכֶלֶת.
— This parallels what Divrei Menachem, by the holy rabbi of Rimanov, says about the verse, “Abraham stretched out his hand and took the knife.”
שֶׁבְּכָל הַמַּעֲשִׂים שֶׁהָיָה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיוּ אֵבָרָיו שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם עוֹשִׂין מֵעַצְמָם מֵרוֹב הַזְּרִיזוּת.
— In every deed that accorded with Hashem’s will, our forefather Abraham’s limbs acted spontaneously through his great alacrity.

וְכֵן הָיָה בְּכָל מַעֲשֵׂה הָעֲקֵידָה, זוּלַת בְּמַעֲשֵׂה לְקִיחַת הַמַּאֲכֶלֶת שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בִּרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁלֹּא רָצָה לְשׁוֹחֲטוֹ; לָכֵן לֹא רָצוּ יָדָיו שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לִיקַּח.
— So it was throughout the Binding, except when taking the knife. That did not accord with His will, for He did not want Abraham to slaughter Isaac; therefore Abraham’s hands did not wish to take it.

רַק אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם חָשַׁד אֶת עַצְמוֹ שֶׁמָּא הוּא מֵהֲסָתַת וְעַצְלוּת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, וְעַל כֵּן כָּתוּב וַיִּשְׁלַח אֶת יָדוֹ, בְּכֹחַ, לִיקַּח אֶת הַמַּאֲכֶלֶת, עַד כָּאן דְּבָרָיו.
— Abraham suspected that this came from the evil inclination’s instigation and laziness. Thus “he stretched out his hand”—forcibly—to take the knife. Here ends the cited teaching.
וְכֵן כָּאן כְּתִיב פֶּן יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ, הַיְינוּ בְּכֹחַ, שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְעוּתָא דְלִבָּא רַק עַל יְדֵי הֲסָתַת הַנָּחָשׁ וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע. וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר:
— Likewise, “lest he stretch out his hand” means forcibly, without the heart’s willing desire, merely through the serpent’s and evil inclination’s instigation. This is the meaning of:
וְלָקַח גַּם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים, גַּם דַּיְיקָא, שֶׁלֹּא יַשְׁלִיךְ מַעֲשָׂיו הָרָעִים, וְיִהְיֶה עֵץ הַחַיִּים טָפֵל.
— “And take also from the Tree of Life”—specifically “also,” without abandoning his evil deeds, so that the Tree of Life would become secondary.
וְאָז יַזִּיק מַה שֶּׁיֹּאכַל מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים, וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר וְלָרָשָׁע אָמַר אֱלֹהִים מַה לְּךָ לְסַפֵּר חוּקָּי וְגוֹמֵר.
— Then eating from the Tree of Life would be harmful, as in the verse, “But to the wicked, God says: What right have you to recount My statutes?” and so forth.
וּכְשֶׁלּוֹמֵד דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְאֵינוֹ מְתַקֵּן מַעֲשָׂיו קוֹדֶם לִהְיוֹת סוּר מֵרָע,
— When someone studies Torah without first rectifying his deeds by turning away from evil,
עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מוֹסִיף כֹּחַ בַּקְּלִיפָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת פח:) לַמַּשְׂמְאִילִים בָּהּ סַמָּא דְמוֹתָא.
— his Torah study adds power to the impure husk, as Shabbat 88b says, “For those who turn left with it, it is a potion of death.”
וְזֶהוּ כְּשֶׁלּוֹמֵד עַל יְדֵי הֲסָתַת הַנָּחָשׁ וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
— This happens when he studies through the serpent’s and evil inclination’s instigation.

h: Two Occurrences and the Third Refinement

p: וְאַחַר שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְשָׁרֵשׁ אַחַר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, יֵשׁ לְהָאָדָם עוֹד עֵסֶק בְּתִיקּוּן עֶטְיוֹ שֶׁל נָחָשׁ.
— After meriting to root out the evil inclination, a person still has the work of rectifying the serpent’s counsel.
וּמִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים, כְּשֶׁמְּבָרֵר עַצְמוֹ בִּב' בְּחִינוֹת, זוֹכֶה לְחַיִּים שֶׁלֹּא בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ לוֹ עֵסֶק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
— “At the end of two full years,” when he refines himself in these two aspects, he attains life without the evil inclination, yet he still has work in this world.
וְהוּא דִּב' מוֹרֶה שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה חֲזָקָה, דְּבִתְרֵי זִמְנֵי נַמִּי מָצִינוּ בַּתּוֹרָה, דִּכְתִיב פֶּן יָמוּת גַּם הוּא כְּאֶחָיו.
— Two indicates an established presumption. The Torah, too, recognizes two occurrences, as it says, “Lest he also die like his brothers.”
וְהוּא פְּלוּגְתָּא דְתַנָּאֵי (יְבָמוֹת סד:) אִי בִּתְרֵי זִמְנֵי הֲוָה חֲזָקָה אוֹ דַּוְקָא בִּתְלָתָא זִמְנֵי.
— The Tannaim dispute (Yevamos 64b) whether a presumption is established after two occurrences or specifically after three.

וְאֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ דִּבְרֵי אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים, שֶׁגַּם בִּב' זִמְנֵי אִתְחֲזַק, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (יוֹמָא פו:): כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָבַר אָדָם עֲבֵירָה וְשָׁנָה בָּהּ וְכוּלֵי נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ כְּהֶיתֵּר, וּמִדָּה טוֹבָה מְרוּבָּה.

— Both are the words of the living God, for two occurrences already establish a pattern. Thus Yoma 86b says that once someone commits a transgression and repeats it, etc., it becomes like something permitted to him. The measure of goodness is greater still.
וּכְשֶׁמְּבָרֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ בִּב' בְּחִינוֹת, מִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים, אָז קֵץ שָׂם לַחֹשֶׁךְ, שֶׁבָּטוּחַ הוּא מֵהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁלוֹט בּוֹ.
— When he refines himself in two aspects, “at the end of two full years,” he “sets an end to darkness”: he is secure against the evil inclination’s rule.

אַךְ מִכָּל מָקוֹם יֵשׁ לוֹ עֵסֶק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה עַד שֶׁיְּבָרֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ בִּבְחִינָה ג', וְאָז הֲוָה חֲזָקָה וְהוּא נִשְׁלָם מִכֹּל וָכֹל וְאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם עֵסֶק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב לֹא אוּכַל עוֹד לָצֵאת וְלָבוֹא.

— Nevertheless, he still has work in this world until he refines himself in a third aspect. Then the presumption becomes established, he is entirely perfected, and he has no further work in this world, as it says, “I can no longer go out and come in.”
וּמִקֵּץ שְׁנָתַיִם יָמִים מוֹרֶה שֶׁנֶּעֱקַר יֵצֶר הָרָע מִלִּבּוֹ, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הָיָה לוֹ עֵסֶק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁרָאִינוּ בְּיוֹסֵף שֶׁחַי אַחַר כָּךְ פ' שָׁנָה.
— “At the end of two full years” indicates that the evil inclination was uprooted from his heart, yet he still had work in this world, as we see with Joseph, who lived another eighty years.
וּכְשֶׁנֶּעֱקַר יֵצֶר הָרָע אֵין אוֹפֶל וְצַלְמָוֶת, שֶׁזֶּה גָּרַם הַנָּחָשׁ.
— When the evil inclination is uprooted, there is no darkness or shadow of death, which the serpent caused.

paragraphs.text: Yevamot 64b: “The Gemara comments: Who is the tanna of the mishna? It is Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who holds that a legal presumption (ḥazaka) is established after two occurrences. As it is taught in a baraita: If a woman circumcised her first son and he died as a result of the circumcision, and she circumcised her second son and he also died, she should not circumcise her third son, as the deaths of the first two produce a presumption that this woman’s sons die as a result of circumcision. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: She should circumcise her third son, as there is not considered to be a legal presumption that her sons die from circumcision, but she should not circumcise her fourth son if her first three sons died from circumcision.”

paragraphs.text: Yoma 86b: “Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says: If one confesses in subsequent years, all the more so is he praiseworthy, as he remembers his earlier sins and is thereby humbled, as it is stated: ‘For I know my transgressions; and my sin is ever before me’ (Psalms 51:5). But how do I establish the meaning of the verse: ‘Like a dog that returns to its vomit’? It may be established in accordance with the opinion of Rav Huna, as Rav Huna said: When a person commits a transgression and repeats it, it is permitted to him. The Gemara is surprised at this: Can it enter your mind that it is permitted to him because he has sinned twice? Rather, say it becomes to him as if it were permitted.”

h: Shabbat and the Light of Chanukah

p: וַאֲכִילַת שַׁבָּת מִסִּטְרָא דְּעֵץ הַחַיִּים, וְהֵם תִּיקּוּן לִפְגַם הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בַּאֲכִילָה.
— Shabbat eating comes from the side of the Tree of Life, and it rectifies the serpent’s blemish, which occurred through eating.
וְהַיְּוָנִים רָצוּ לְהַשְׁכִּיחָם תּוֹרָתֶךָ, שֶׁכֵּן אוֹתִיּוֹת הַחֹשֶׁךְ הוּא שִׁכְחָה.
— The Greeks sought “to make them forget Your Torah,” for the letters of הַחֹשֶׁךְ, “the darkness,” also form שִׁכְחָה, “forgetfulness.”
וּבִבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה נִדְרָשׁ וְחוֹשֶׁךְ זֶה יָוָן, שֶׁהֶחְשִׁיכָה עֵינֵיהֶם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁכָּל הַגְּזֵירוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם הָיָה לְבַטֵּל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
— Bereishis Rabbah interprets “and darkness” as Greece, which darkened Israel’s eyes; all its decrees sought to suppress Torah.
וְעַל יְדֵי כֹּהֲנֶיךָ הַקְּדוֹשִׁים זָכוּ לָאוֹר, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת זָכוֹר, אֲתַר דְּלֵית לֵיהּ שִׁכְחָה וְלֹא קַיְימָא בֵּיהּ שִׁכְחָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב צב ב).
— Through “Your holy kohanim” they attained light, the aspect of remembrance: a place that has no forgetfulness and where forgetfulness cannot exist, as the holy Zohar states (II, 92b).

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 2:4: “… ‘And disorder (vavohu)’ – this is the Median kingdom, (as it is stated:) ‘They hastened (vayavhilu) to bring Haman’ (Esther 6:14). ‘And darkness’– this is the Greek kingdom, which darkened Israel’s eyes with their edicts, as they used to say to them: ‘Write on the horn of a bull that you have no portion in the God of Israel.’ ‘Upon the face of the depths’ – this is the evil kingdom (Edom), which cannot be calculated, like the depths; just as the depths cannot be calculated, so is it with (the wickedness of) the wicked. ‘And the spirit of God was hovering’ – this is the spirit of the messianic king, as it says: ‘The spirit of the Lord will rest upon him’ (Isaiah 11:2). …”
